front: What does part 3 of the PLC standard IEC 61131, written IEC 61131-3, deal with?
back: The basic software architecture and the programming languages of a controller's control program.
excerpt: Part 3 of IEC 61131 deals with basic software architecture and programming languages of the control program within PLC.
mnemonic: Part 3 is the software part: how a control program is built and which languages it is written in.

front: What does the abbreviation POU stand for in IEC 61131-3?
excerpt: variables of system-defined Program Organization Units (POUs, see below)
mnemonic: A Program is Organized into Units: Program Organization Unit.

front: Which three kinds of program organization unit (POU) does IEC 61131-3 list?
excerpt: Functions Standard: ADD, SQRT, SIN, COS, GT, MIN, MAX, AND, OR, etc. Custom Function Blocks Standard: Custom – Libraries of functions can be supplied by a vendor or third party. Programs
mnemonic: Three units, growing in memory: a function forgets, a function block remembers per instance, a program remembers once for everyone.

front: Why does a function (FUNCTION) keep no values from one call to the next?
back: All its data are temporary stack variables: valid only while it executes and re-initialized each time it is called.
excerpt: All data of a function are temporary and are only valid while the function is executed (stack variables). This means that TwinCAT re-initializes all variables that you have declared in a function each time the function is called.
mnemonic: A function is a goldfish: every call it starts again with a blank memory.

front: What does a function block retain between executions that a function does not?
back: The values of its output variables and its internal variables, until the next execution.
excerpt: The values of the output variables and the internal variables are retained until the next execution.
mnemonic: Function = goldfish, function block = elephant: the block still remembers its outputs and internal variables at the next call.

front: What is an instance of a function block?
back: A copy of the function block; the function block is always called through such an instance.
excerpt: A function block is always called via an instance, which is a copy of the function block.
mnemonic: The function block is the cookie cutter, each instance is a cookie: you only ever use the cookies, never the cutter itself.

front: From outside a function block instance, which of its variables can you access?
back: Only its input and output variables, not its internal variables.
excerpt: From outside the function block instance, you can only access input and output variables of a function block, not the internal variables.
mnemonic: A function block is a vending machine: you reach the coin slot (inputs) and the tray (outputs), never the mechanism inside.

front: How does a program differ from a function block with respect to instances?
back: A program has no instances: it has one set of values, retained between calls whichever unit calls it.
excerpt: Programs do not have instances. If a POU calls a program and the call results in changes to the values of the program, the changes are retained until the next program call.
mnemonic: A program is one shared whiteboard: every caller sees what the last caller left. Function blocks hand each instance its own notebook.

front: In the IEC 61131-3 configuration model, in which three ways can a program be executed?
back: Once, on a timer, or on an event.
excerpt: Can be executed once, on a timer, on an event.
mnemonic: Think of an alarm clock: one shot (once), repeating alarm (timer), or the doorbell ringing (event).

front: How far does the visibility of a global variable (VAR_GLOBAL) reach in a PLC project?
back: Throughout the whole project: every part of it knows the global variable.
excerpt: variables, constants, or retentive variables that are known throughout the project. Global variables are declared in global variable lists between the keywords VAR_GLOBAL and END_VAR.
mnemonic: GLOBAL = the whole globe of your project can see it.

front: What happens to the value of a RETAIN variable after a power failure?
back: It is kept: when the program restarts, the system continues to operate with the stored value.
excerpt: RETAIN variables retain their value after an uncontrolled termination (power failure). When the program restarts, the system continues to operate with the stored values.
mnemonic: RETAIN = the part counter that still knows its count after the lights went out.
